C. Recommended Alternative
The alignment studies for Lincoln Highway were made after full and careful consideration of the existing Comprehensive Plans of the Villages of Park Forest, Matteson, and Olympia Fields as well as that of the city of Chicago Heights.
Land-use characteristics in the plans were assessed and the effect of the Lincoln Highway improvement was considered. The alternate alignments proposed for this improvement will produce no need for changes in the existing plans. Land-use patterns outlined by the plans were presently being developed and the proposed improvement will assist the full implementation of the plans.
Park lands contemplated by the Comprehensive Plans will not be compromised by this improvement.
The existing neighborhoods and their forecasted composition will remain as planned under the alignment proposals in this report, since the highway will remain in its present location.
Alignment B was laid out in an attempt to minimize the disruption to existing land use by shifting the centerline for the improvement away from the built-up side of the existing roadway in those areas where one side of the right-of-way was open and undeveloped. During the course of the study, however, subdivisions were created and development took place that mitigated the opportunities sought by this alignment.
Alignment A was designed to place the proposed new centerline generally along the existing centerline, and therefore necessitates comparable takings along both sides of the existing roadway. These required takings, however, are approximately one-half as wide as those that would be needed under the concept of Line B.
